title: Vitamin C and the common cold
abstract: Regular vitamin C supplementation does not reduce the incidence of colds in the general population.
Supplementation slightly shortens the duration of cold symptoms in adults by about 8 percent.
Very high doses taken after symptoms start show no consistent benefit.

title: Aspirin for secondary prevention
abstract: Low-dose aspirin reduces the risk of a second heart attack in patients with cardiovascular disease.
The usual preventive dose is 75 to 100 mg per day.
Aspirin increases the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.

title: Sleep duration and memory
abstract: Adults who sleep less than 6 hours per night perform worse on memory consolidation tasks.
Slow-wave sleep is associated with the transfer of memories to the cortex.
A short nap of 20 minutes improves alertness in the afternoon.

title: Statins and cholesterol
abstract: Statins lower LDL cholesterol by inhibiting the enzyme HMG-CoA reductase.
A moderate dose reduces LDL cholesterol by 30 to 40 percent.
Muscle pain is reported by a minority of patients.

title: Antibiotics and viral infections
abstract: Antibiotics are not effective against viral infections such as influenza.
Unnecessary antibiotic use increases bacterial resistance.
Most sore throats in adults are caused by viruses.

title: Exercise and type 2 diabetes
abstract: Regular aerobic exercise improves insulin sensitivity in patients with type 2 diabetes.
A programme of 150 minutes per week lowers HbA1c by about 0.6 percentage points.
Resistance training provides additional benefit.

title: Caffeine and alertness
abstract: Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors in the brain, which increases alertness.
The half-life of caffeine in healthy adults is about 5 hours.
Caffeine intake late in the day delays sleep onset.

title: Smoking and lung cancer
abstract: Tobacco smoking is the main cause of lung cancer and accounts for about 85 percent of cases.
The risk decreases progressively after smoking cessation.
Passive smoking also increases the risk in non-smokers.

title: Vitamin D and bone health
abstract: Vitamin D promotes the absorption of calcium in the intestine.
Severe deficiency causes rickets in children.
Supplementation alone does not prevent fractures in healthy adults.

title: Hand washing and infections
abstract: Hand washing with soap reduces the incidence of diarrhoeal disease by about 30 percent.
Alcohol-based hand rub is effective against most bacteria.
Hand hygiene compliance in hospitals is often below 50 percent.

title: Blood pressure and salt
abstract: A high sodium intake is associated with higher blood pressure.
Reducing salt intake by 4 grams per day lowers systolic blood pressure by about 5 mmHg in hypertensive patients.
Potassium intake has the opposite effect.

title: Mediterranean diet
abstract: The Mediterranean diet is rich in olive oil, vegetables and fish.
It is associated with a lower risk of cardiovascular events.
Adherence is measured with a 14-item questionnaire.
